version_note: The first formal attempt used one Python interpreter for serial windows and exited natively during middle-load crosslink_4x/canonical/seed0. Its log and partial trace remain under runs/formal. Formal V2 uses an independent interpreter per cell; physics, schedulers, cells, seeds, metrics, and thresholds are unchanged.
question: Does the best fixed path space change with offered load or cross-cluster link capacity on the same heterogeneous GPU topology?
scope: C1_multi / frozen 24-GPU three-cluster placement only; this validates motivation for dynamic path control and does not validate an adaptive controller.

path_spaces: partial: canonical transitions plus the four frozen nominal-network slow-link bypass edges from v3_gated_pathspace/audit.json
full: all layer-compatible physical DAG edges
frozen.network_intervention: Scale the bandwidth of compute-to-compute links whose nominal capacity is <= 50,000,000 B/s; keep link latency, all other links, NIC capacities, placement, M3 costs, and the partial edge set fixed.
frozen.kv_admission: Use the same full-lifetime prompt-plus-1000-output-token reservation and completion wakeup for all path spaces.

formal.execution: one fresh Python process per window

analysis.primary_metric: P95 TPOT, with output throughput and completion fraction as guardrails; also report P95 TTFT, end backlog, common-completed request tails, path use, Decode batch size, and KV reservation utilization.
analysis.trace_pairing: For each load and seed, all six path-space/network cells must have the exact same trace hash.
analysis.descriptive_winner: A unique winner is reported only if it has the lowest three-seed mean P95 TPOT, mean output throughput at least 99% of the best policy, mean completion fraction no more than 1 percentage point below the best policy, and its mean P95 TPOT is at least 1% lower than the next eligible policy. Otherwise report a latency-throughput tradeoff or tie.
analysis.crossover: Evidence for changing path-space preference requires different unique winners across load or network conditions and a matching directional preference in at least two of the three paired seeds. Three seeds are descriptive, not a significance test.
analysis.negative_result: If one fixed path space remains the unique winner throughout the tested matrix, this experiment does not support a path-space-switching motivation for Work 3 in the tested range.

failure_policy: Preserve failures and logs; do not replace seeds or impute failed metrics. Any missing or trace-mismatched formal cell prevents a complete crossover claim.
